date_note: The Record (dated 20 November) quotes a House of Delegates official saying the attack started on Thursday; 19 November is Thursday.
exec: A state legislature's website and IT systems are down, which can disrupt public access to lawmaking.
geo_basis: state legislature seat (Charleston); the source gives no city
impact: The Record reports the Legislature's website is down and IT systems are affected; an official said access to certain Legislature IT systems was temporarily disabled.
plain: The West Virginia Legislature's website and some of its computer systems are affected by a cyber incident, The Record reports. An official says other state agencies are not affected.
summary: Ann Ali, deputy chief of staff for the West Virginia House of Delegates, told The Record the attack started on Thursday and continued through Friday, and that access to certain Legislature IT systems has been temporarily disabled. She said teams began an investigation with outside specialists and that no other state agencies are affected. No hacking group had claimed it as of Friday.
title: West Virginia Legislature hit with cyber incident affecting IT systems

validation.note: The Record read. West Virginia Watch's report could not be read (HTTP 403), so it is not cited; the Legislature's statement is quoted by The Record only.

review.note: Checked title, date, Ali quotes, no other agencies, no group claim against The Record. Plain and impact presented the website outage as the Legislature statement (reporter wording): reattributed. Action had advice not in the source: now awareness only.
